transcript: You are running out of time to see some of the best theatre in New York! So here is a time sensitive round up of shows closing before the end of November. And I'm including two categories of shows here, ones that I already saw and enjoyed and ones that I have tickets to see before they close. We've got nothing can take you from the hand of god, about a lesbian author who returns to her rural, religious hometown to confront her past. I’ve had a tough time recommending this to people only because it sounds like tickets in New York are somewhat overpriced, whereas I saw it for a more reasonable price in London. But if the tickets are in your price range, I have to say I thought this was a pretty exhilarating experience. This one is going to end performances on November 23rd. This one is performed in a centuries old library that was shipped from Italy and it's a pretty light hearted, silly classical comedy. I'm super excited for this brief concert run of The Sweet Smell of success by MasterVoices. And it's gonna be starring at Raul Esparza, Lizzy McAlpine and a great cast all around. A new adaptation of pride and prejudice that's still a period piece, but is written and directed with this fresh, contemporary flare. And then there's four more that I'm planning to see this month. We have The Seat of Our Pants, a new musical based on the Thornton Wilder play The Skin of Our Teeth. I've already heard some divisive things about this from previews, but I really like the writer, Ethan Lipton. He has a really kooky, out there brand of humor I like the play that it's based on, so I'm still very excited to see this for myself. Also at the Public is initiative, a new coming of age play which is five hours long, which for some people might be a deterrent, but for me, I'm ready for the marathon. Then there's The Burning Cauldron of Fiery Fire by Anne Washburn, which I think I'm gonna love. The marketing describes it as “a tender,  funny, probing story about a death, a pageant, a rescue, a resurrection, pigs, and the act of saying Grace. So that's my list, but let me know if there's anything else on your radar that's closing before the end of November.
